posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked:
8-tracks, vinyl, and cassettes when I was growing up. 

I remember how excited we were when CDs came out while we were in college. We had seven of us in our apartment: one person bought a player, everyone bought their own CDs, and we took turns playing them. It was great! 

I think the quality has gotten better (depending on the situation), although I think listening to Alan Parson's Tales of Mystery and Imagination on a headset via cassette is just as good as CD...

posts.name: Sonvar
posts.cooked: Cassettes, CDs, and then mp3s.  Honestly I can’t tell a difference in quality.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: Same as Powerhound - had cassettes when I was a kid, then aged into CDs and now MP3s. Although add in ye-olde-fashioned records into that as well, as my parents have a fairly large collection between them and we had a hi-fi system thing with a record player so I got to listen to a bunch of those as a kid too.

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked:
Vinyl were still around when I was growing up, but cassettes were the new medium and soon took over. So much time spent with a pencil trying to spool that magnetic tape back in, I do not miss that! I can remember when CDs where thought of as the thing "the rich kid" had, and magazines were printing articles like "10 things to do with your CDs when they are scratched. 1. A coaster.". Dark times.

I've never noticed a difference in quality over the mediums.

 

New day, new questions!

Too much or too little? Would you rather have access to a thing but not enough to satisfy you or so much that it becomes boring to have it all the time?

posts.name: Sonvar
posts.cooked: Probably limited access though I’d likely complain.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: I suppose it depends what it is. I mean, if it's something like people to play games with, I'm already in the former category. If it was something like food, I'd rather have the latter ;).

posts.name: Phantom5613
posts.cooked:
If it's something non-essential like episodes of a tv show or , then too little.

If I need it to live, then I'm pretty sure anyone would say they'd rather have too much.

posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked: Agreed, I've seen plenty of media that I lose interest in and think I could pinpoint exactly the spot where it should have stopped...though I didn't know it at the time. Makes me look back at the things that were "cut short" more positively!

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked:
I'd rather have too little than too much and become bored of it. Boredom is my enemy and must be quashed!

fjur’s Questions of the Day #2: Would you rather go to the Past or the Future? (You can go to multiple different Times in either one you choose, you can stay any amount of time in any time, and you can return to the Present.)

posts.cooked: I’m a pessimist so I’ll say past.

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked: I’d go past - so many questions I’d like to find answers to…

posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked: It would be fascinating to get a glimpse of the future – but I would rather go far future, hundreds or thousands of years, than the near future. My goal is to satisfy my curiosity, not shape my sports betting!

posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked: The future. Surely if I can go to the future then someone in said future would have found a way to send me to the past. Plus, I can big the people that out lived me!

My Answer to Yesterday’s Question: I think I’d probably rather go to the future, because I wouldn’t want to accidentally mess-up the past via the Butterfly Effect and come home to a different present.
